findings.issue: The translation preserves the death prediction but drops the emphatic cognate construction, literally “will die by death.” Neither the text nor note b represents this source-backed emphasis.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “will surely die,” with a note identifying the emphatic Greek construction. Review that proposed rendering before adoption.

findings.source_quote: ἀλλὰ καὶ τούτοις, [φησίν,] ἐπίκειται μετάνοια. βλέπεις, [φησί,] τινὰς ἐξ αὐτῶν μετανενοηκότας. καὶ ἔτι, φησίν, ἐστὶν ἐν αὐτοῖς ἐλπὶς μετανοίας.
findings.english_quote: Yet repentance is offered to these too. You see that some have repented, and they still have hope of repentance.
findings.issue: The reporting expressions are omitted without disclosure. This conceals the working edition’s distinction between bracketed editorial supplements, [φησίν,] and [φησί,], and the unbracketed φησίν. The unbracketed reporting expression in paragraph 3 is also omitted. The quotation formatting does not misidentify the speaker, but it does not preserve or disclose these source distinctions.
findings.suggested_revision: Represent the unbracketed “he says” expressions in paragraphs 2 and 3, and explain separately that the working edition brackets the first two reporting expressions in paragraph 2 as editorial supplements. Do not present those supplements as unmarked preserved wording.

findings.source_quote: καὶ ὅσοι, φησίν, ἐξ αὐτῶν μετανενοήκασι, τὴν κατοικίαν εἰς τὸν πύργον ἔχουσιν·
findings.english_quote: Retain each rod group, response conditions, renewed seal and plural spirits; select sinners with declared Athos and partial Michigan evidence.
findings.issue: The theological metadata attributes decisions about a renewed seal, plural spirits, and a sinners reading to this unit. None occurs in the selected source. The supplied evidence locates the sinners selection in S.8.vi.6, not S.8.vii. This is inaccurate per-unit provenance, even though those matters may belong to surrounding material.
findings.suggested_revision: Replace this metadata with a unit-specific account of the rod groups, repentance timing, tower/walls distinction, renewed division, and life/death assertions. Move any neighboring-unit decisions to their actual records or identify them explicitly as cross-unit background.

findings.source_quote: Ὅσοι δὲ ἡμιξήρους ἐπέδωκαν καὶ ἐν αὐταῖς σχισμὰς εἶχον, ἄκουε καὶ περὶ αὐτῶν.
findings.english_quote: Listen also about the people whose rods were half dry and cracked.
findings.issue: The simplified opening omits the act of handing in the rods, expressed by ἐπέδωκαν. It identifies only their condition. Paragraph 4 likewise replaces the people who handed in green, cracked rods with people whose rods had that condition.
findings.suggested_revision: Restore the submission action in both places, for example “Listen also about the people who handed in half-dry, cracked rods” and “The people who handed in green, cracked rods …”. Review these proposals directly against the Greek.

findings.issue: The source addresses the hearer directly: “You see some of them who have repented.” The simplified text omits that appeal to visible evidence and makes an unqualified statement instead.
findings.suggested_revision: Restore the direct address and group reference, for example “You see that some of them have repented.” Disclose the bracketed reporting expression separately.

findings.source_quote: καὶ ἔτι, φησίν, ἐστὶν ἐν αὐτοῖς ἐλπὶς μετανοίας.
findings.english_quote: They still have hope of repentance.
findings.issue: The unbracketed reporting expression φησίν is omitted, as is its counterpart in paragraph 3. No note distinguishes these unbracketed expressions from the two bracketed editorial supplements in paragraph 2. Speaker identity remains consistent, but the source’s reporting structure and editorial status are undisclosed.
findings.suggested_revision: Represent the unbracketed reporting expressions and add a concise disclosure identifying the bracketed expressions as supplements in the working edition, rather than treating all reporting expressions alike.

findings.issue: The simplified text independently drops the emphatic cognate death construction. Its agreement with the standard edition does not establish fidelity to this source-backed emphasis.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “will surely die,” retaining a short explanation of the emphatic Greek wording. This proposal requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: καὶ ὅσοι, φησίν, ἐξ αὐτῶν μετανενοήκασι, τὴν κατοικίαν εἰς τὸν πύργον ἔχουσιν·
findings.english_quote: Retain each rod group, response conditions, renewed seal and plural spirits; select sinners with declared Athos and partial Michigan evidence.
findings.issue: The theological metadata claims decisions about a renewed seal, plural spirits, and a sinners reading that are absent from this unit. The supplied evidence places the sinners selection in S.8.vi.6. The simplification metadata repeats the same contamination by claiming to retain “renewed seal and plural spirits, sinners noun.”
findings.suggested_revision: Revise both metadata blocks to describe only decisions actually present in S.8.vii. Identify neighboring-unit matters as cross-unit background if they must be retained.

summary: Both editions require revision. They preserve the principal rod groups, repentance timing, tower/walls distinction, negations, and conditional life/death warnings, and their repentance terminology fits current policy. Necessary repairs concern emphatic death wording, omitted source features, undisclosed editorial supplements, and inaccurate unit-specific metadata. The simplified edition additionally omits rod submission and the direct “you see” appeal. The disclosed working readings should not be replaced merely because alternatives exist. This review evaluates the supplied source and attributed reports; it does not authenticate unseen manuscripts or certify an exhaustive collation.
